attempts.rationale: Test a robust weighted combination using inverse_error weights on the full pool to leverage the unstable ranking and trend dominance.
Testing a simple mean combination to see if a robust unweighted approach beats the weighted inverse_error baseline, given the unstable ranking and trend dominance.
test a softmax_neg_error weighted combination to see if a more aggressive weighting improves over inverse_error, given unstable ranking.
The series has unstable ranking and strong trend; a simple robust estimator like median may be competitive against weighted schemes.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a robust DBA (dynamic best‑average) might adapt better than static weighted schemes.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking, so a robust trimmed mean may outperform simple mean while reducing influence of high‑error models.
test a weighted scheme with no shrinkage (inverse_error, concentration 0) to see if more variance helps under unstable ranking.
The series has unstable ranking and strong trend; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting may capture changing dominance over horizons.
use softmax weights on the top‑5 models to reduce influence of noisy models
trend-dominated with unstable ranking suggests a simple robust mean over the top 5 models may compete with weighted; test a mean on pool4.
Test a robust weighted combination on the stable 5‑model pool using inverse_error weights to see if simple weighting beats the softmax variant.
Test a robust estimator on the top‑5 pool to see if median beats weighted; trend dominance suggests simple robust combine may help.

decision.justification: Selected 'median on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9551. Series context: trend strength 0.6137 and seasonal strength 0.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.166); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.451.
